P1_purpose_aptness.medium: Since 1999, the Fourth Plinth in London’s Trafalgar Square, a pedestal originally intended for an equestrian statue, has displayed commissions by contemporary artists. The square commemorates Horatio Nelson’s 1805 naval victory at Trafalgar, and his statue presides over it from atop a monumental column. ______ British Nigerian artist Yinka Shonibare’s 2010 commission was a scale replica of Nelson’s flagship, HMS Victory, sealed inside a giant bottle.
A1_addition.medium: Conservation biologist Samuel Wasser traces ivory trafficking by comparing DNA from confiscated tusks with a genetic reference map built from samples of elephant dung, skin, and hair collected across Africa, an approach that reveals where poaching is concentrated. ______ his team searches separate seizures for the two tusks of a single elephant: a match indicates that both shipments originated with the same dealer.
S1_spec_restate.medium: In a 2016 study, plant biologist Stacey Harmer and her colleagues showed that a circadian clock controls heliotropism in young sunflowers—______ the plants’ stems bend over the course of each day so that the buds follow the Sun from east to west. Once the flowers mature, however, they stop moving and face east.
T1_sequence_time.medium: Rearing Pacific bluefin tuna from the eggs of captive-raised parents defeated many research institutes: in hatchery tanks, larvae cannibalized one another, and juveniles frequently died after colliding with the walls. Japan’s Kindai University, which began investigating the species in 1970, persisted after other programs had abandoned the effort. ______ in 2002, its researchers produced the world’s first fully farm-raised bluefin.
U1_culmination_alt.medium: Cosmic rays, which continuously bombard Earth’s surface, generate background signals that can obscure the exceedingly rare particle interactions sought by dark matter experiments. China’s Jinping Underground Laboratory, inaugurated in 2010 midway along a road tunnel in Sichuan Province, lies beneath 2,400 meters of marble; ______ the PandaX experiment monitors liquid xenon for the faint recoil of atomic nuclei struck by dark matter particles.
C1_two_subject.hard: Researchers disagree about how farming can coexist with wildlife. Surveying birds and trees in Ghana and India, Ben Phalan and colleagues concluded in 2011 that most species fare best when crops are grown intensively on minimal land, leaving more forest intact; ______ ecologists Ivette Perfecto and John Vandermeer contend that biodiversity depends chiefly on the quality of the farmland between forest fragments, through which species move.
C3_limiting_fact.hard: Malian singer Oumou Sangaré built her sound on wassoulou, a style rooted in the pentatonic songs of her mother’s home region in southern Mali and anchored by the kamalengoni, a harp adapted in the 1960s from the instrument of Wassoulou hunters. Her lyrics, ______ have challenged social conventions long accepted there: her 1989 debut album, Moussolou (“Women”), warned listeners against polygamy and forced marriage.
K1_grant_turn.hard: The paintings that senior men began producing in 1971 at Papunya, a settlement in Australia’s Western Desert, extended a visual tradition far older than the settlement itself. ______ their medium was new: the acrylic paints distributed by schoolteacher Geoffrey Bardon and the scraps of building board they painted on had no precedent in the region’s art. Yet the designs came from ceremonial body painting and sand mosaics.
K2_qualification.hard: Because white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are more energy efficient than the yellow high-pressure sodium lamps long used to light roads, municipalities worldwide are converting their streetlights to LEDs. ______ the transition may intensify the ecological effects of light pollution. In a 2014 study, Stephen Pawson and Martin Bader found that LED-fitted light traps captured, on average, 48 percent more insects than traps with sodium lamps.
E1_consequence.hard: In 2014, a team led by Morten Allentoft analyzed ancient DNA from 281 moa, the giant flightless birds that vanished from New Zealand after Polynesian settlement in the late thirteenth century. In all four species studied, the DNA revealed large populations whose genetic diversity held steady for the 4,000 years before the extinction. Claims that moa were already declining before humans arrived, ______ appear unfounded.
P1_purpose_aptness.hard: German architect Anna Heringer meant the school she designed for the Bangladeshi village of Rudrapur to serve the local economy as well as its pupils: the construction budget, she argued, should stay with villagers rather than flow to outside industries such as cement manufacturing. ______ the METI school, completed in 2005, was built largely by local craftspeople and villagers from earth, straw, and bamboo.
A1_addition.hard: Drawing on years of interviews with her parents, Thi Bui reconstructs their lives in Vietnam in her 2017 graphic memoir The Best We Could Do, from their very different childhoods, his impoverished and hers privileged, to the family’s escape by boat after the war. ______ the book chronicles Bui’s own early motherhood in New York. Her son’s birth prompts her to reexamine what her parents endured.
S1_spec_restate.hard: Integrative Science, a program launched at Cape Breton University in 1999, sought to combine Indigenous and Western sciences within a single curriculum. In 2004, Mi’kmaw Elder Albert Marshall articulated its guiding principle, Etuaptmumk, or Two-Eyed Seeing. ______ learners were to view the world with one eye attuned to the strengths of Indigenous knowledge and the other attuned to those of Western science, using both perspectives simultaneously.
M1_emphasis.hard: In 2021, researchers Lyubov Shmakova and Stas Malavin reported that a bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal, had revived from Siberian permafrost about 24,000 years old and then reproduced in the laboratory. The finding vastly extended the known limits of rotifer survival in a frozen state. ______ earlier reports had documented rotifers surviving for only six to ten years when frozen.
U1_culmination_alt.hard: Chinese artist Song Dong assembled Waste Not in 2005 from more than 10,000 objects his mother had saved over five decades, hoping the project would ease her grief after his father’s death in 2002. Though it began as a private consolation, ______ the installation came to be seen as a portrait of a generation for whom thrift had been a strategy for surviving decades of political upheaval.
